title: Timed universal nondeterministic simulation
statement: For every effective code for finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machines with two work tapes, there is a finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machine $U_N$ such that, for each Boolean string $\alpha$, some natural number $C$ works for every Boolean string $x$ and every natural number $t$. On input $\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, every choice sequence of length exactly $C(t+1)$ causes $U_N$ to halt. Moreover, $U_N$ has an accepting computation of exactly that length if and only if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ has an accepting computation on $x$ using exactly $t$ nondeterministic choices.
hypotheses_covered: An effective code for finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machines with two work tapes
For each $\alpha$, a natural number $C$ is chosen independently of $x$ and $t$
The input is the nested pairing $\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$
Every choice sequence of length exactly $C(t+1)$ leads to halting
Acceptance by the universal machine is existential over choice sequences of exactly that length
The decoded machine's acceptance is by a choice sequence of exactly $t$ choices
